instantiated_cells.justification: The statutes define lobbying/advocacy as direct communications to promote/oppose/influence legislation (§101.70(E)), executive agency decisions (§121.60(I)), and retirement system decisions (§101.90(I)).

Ohio defines three lobbyist categories as persons/individuals engaged to actively advocate as a main purpose (legislative agent), to influence executive agency decisions as a main purpose on a regular and substantial basis (executive agency lobbyist), and to influence retirement system decisions similarly (retirement system lobbyist).
The definition of "person" expressly includes state instrumentalities and political subdivisions such as counties, townships, municipal corporations, and school districts.

Both the executive agency lobbyist and retirement system lobbyist definitions require lobbying as a main purpose on a "regular and substantial basis," which functions as a materiality/substantiality threshold.

Executive agency lobbying is defined as influencing "executive agency decisions" by direct communication with officials of an "executive agency," which is broadly defined to include offices/departments/boards/commissions under elected executive officials.
The executive agency lobbying expenditure/target definitions include "a member of the staff" of covered officials, and "staff" is defined for executive agencies in §121.60(M).
"Actively advocate" includes direct communication with the governor (and staff), making the governor's office an explicit lobbying target.

"Executive agency" includes "any other state agency, department, board, or commission" controlled/directed by an elected executive official or subject to that official's authority, covering many non-departmental boards/commissions.
Legislative lobbying targets matters pending before the general assembly and includes direct communication with members of the general assembly to influence legislation.
"Actively advocate" includes direct communication with "any member of the staff" of listed officials, and "staff" is defined in §101.70(J).

Each lobbyist definition excludes certain elected/appointed officials (e.g., legislative agent excludes members of the general assembly and statewide elected executives; executive/retirement lobbyist excludes elected/appointed government officers/employees acting in a fiduciary capacity), so elected officials are not within the defined lobbyist actor class.

instantiated_cells.cited_section: Ohio Rev. Code § 121.60(H); Ohio Rev. Code § 101.90(H)
instantiated_cells.justification: The executive agency lobbyist and retirement system lobbyist definitions exclude officers or employees of federal/state agencies or political subdivisions acting in a fiduciary capacity, meaning public employees are not categorically included as lobbyists.
The statute defines covered governmental entities by type (state instrumentalities and political subdivisions) and does not condition the definition on any charter-based test.
The governmental/public-entity inclusions in "person" are categorical and do not turn on any ownership or control percentage test.
The definition of "person" includes enumerated governmental bodies without reference to revenue sources or a revenue-structure criterion.
